## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

import { existsSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync, mkdirSync, statSync } from 'node:fs'
import { resolve, join, extname } from 'node:path'
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
import { createServer } from 'node:http'
import { spawn } from 'node:child_process'
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url'
import { child } from './session-lifecycle.mjs'
import { livePreviewScript, watchProject } from './live-preview.mjs'

export function projectType(root) {
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'package.json'))) {
    const p = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'), 'utf8'))
    if (p.dependencies?.next || p.devDependencies?.next) throw new Error('Unsupported framework: customize start.sh and provide static deployment output.')
    if (p.dependencies?.vite || p.devDependencies?.vite) return 'vite'
    throw new Error('Unsupported package project: customize start.sh and deployment output.')
  }
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) return 'html'
  throw new Error('No generated index.html or supported package project.')
}
export async function start(root = process.cwd()) {
  const type = projectType(root)
  const projectRoot = resolve(root)
  if (type === 'vite') {
    const stampDir = process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR || join(root, 'node_modules', '.cache')
    mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
    const stamp = join(stampDir, 'default-dependencies')
    const lock = join(root, 'package-lock.json')
    const hash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
    let old = ''
    try { old = readFileSync(stamp, 'utf8') } catch {}
    if (old !== hash || !existsSync(join(root, 'node_modules/vite'))) {
      await child('npm', [existsSync(lock) ? 'ci' : 'install', '--no-audit', '--no-fund'], { cwd: root })
      mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
      const installedHash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
      writeFileSync(stamp, installedHash)
    }
    await child(process.execPath, [join(root, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './'], { cwd: root })
    root = join(root, 'dist')
  }
  if (!existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) throw new Error('Static deployment output must contain index.html.')
  if (process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR) writeFileSync(join(process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR, 'deployment-output.json'), JSON.stringify({ project: projectRoot, directory: resolve(root) }))
  const mime = { '.html':'text/html', '.js':'application/javascript', '.css':'text/css', '.json':'application/json', '.svg':'image/svg+xml', '.png':'image/png', '.jpg':'image/jpeg', '.webp':'image/webp', '.wasm':'application/wasm', '.glb':'model/gltf-binary' }
  const clients = new Set()
  const stopWatching = watchProject(root, () => { for (const client of clients) client.write('event: change\ndata: changed\n\n') })
  const keepAlive = setInterval(() => { for (const client of clients) client.write(': keepalive\n\n') }, 20000)
  const buildWatcher = type === 'vite' ? spawn(process.execPath, [join(projectRoot, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './', '--watch'], { cwd: projectRoot, stdio: 'inherit' }) : null
  const server = createServer((req, res) => {
    try {
      const url = new URL(req.url, 'http://localhost')
      if (url.pathname === '/__omgithub/live') {
        res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream', 'Cache-Control': 'no-cache', 'X-Accel-Buffering': 'no', Connection: 'keep-alive' })
        res.write(': connected\n\n')
        clients.add(res)
        req.on('close', () => clients.delete(res))
        return
      }
      const path = resolve(root, '.' + decodeURIComponent(url.pathname))
      if (path !== resolve(root) && !path.startsWith(resolve(root) + '/')) { res.writeHead(404); res.end(); return }
      const file = statSync(path).isDirectory() ? join(path, 'index.html') : path
      res.setHeader('Content-Type', mime[extname(file)] || 'application/octet-stream')
      res.setHeader('Cache-Control', url.searchParams.has('omgithub_live') ? 'no-store' : 'no-cache')
      const content = readFileSync(file)
      if (extname(file) === '.html' && url.searchParams.get('omgithub_live') === '1') {
        const html = content.toString()
        res.end(/<\/body\s*>/i.test(html) ? html.replace(/<\/body\s*>/i, `${livePreviewScript}</body>`) : html + livePreviewScript)
      } else res.end(content)
    } catch { res.writeHead(404); res.end('Not found') }
  })
  server.on('close', () => { stopWatching(); clearInterval(keepAlive); buildWatcher?.kill(); for (const client of clients) client.end() })
  server.listen(Number(process.env.PORT || 3000), '0.0.0.0')

Good: static HTML at root is supported; server runs at PORT or 3000. I'll build a static vanilla JS game.

Now design the game carefully.

**Concept: "VANISHING POINT" / "The Long Haul"** — Oregon Trail-like road trip from San Francisco to Atlantic City with a van and a crew of unique-skilled people. 2D, phone/tablet portrait/landscape responsive.

Key design:
- Start screen: title, New Run, How to Play, maybe difficulty.
- Crew select: choose 4 from 8 characters with skills (Mechanic, Medic, Navigator, Cook, Negotiator, Scout, Musician/Entertainer, Hacker/Electronics). Each has traits/perks and quirks. Start with limited equipment.
- Resource management: fuel, food, water, money, van condition, morale, tires, spare parts, medicine. Maybe simplify to fuel, food, water, condition, morale, cash, medkits, spare tire. Distance progress from SF to Atlantic City (~2,700 miles) along route with cities/landmarks.
- Map journey: stylized 2D route with stops (SF → Sacramento → Reno → Salt Lake → Denver → Kansas City → St. Louis → Chicago → Cleveland → Pittsburgh → Philadelphia → Atlantic City). Or Route 66-ish then east.
- Gameplay loop: each "leg" between stops is a day; choose travel pace (cautious/normal/push), manage rations, interact with event cards requiring skills. Events offer choices with skill checks; character skills give success chances/extra options. Consequences consume resources, injure crew, damage van, etc.
- Camp/rest, scavenge, work for cash, repair van, trade at stops. Shop to buy fuel/food/parts.
- Random events with art (CSS/SVG illustrations rather than external images). Need visual quality. We can create procedural SVG scenes for each event? A rich 2D aesthetic: sunset highway, van side view, parallax background, day/night cycle. Use canvas for the road animation? Could be effective: a horizontal side-scrolling van driving scene with parallax mountains/desert/city, animated road; van depiction via SVG sprite with wheels rotating. Then event cards overlay.

Phone/tablet 2D: layout should be responsive. Design for portrait-first, works landscape.

Goal: challenging, most runs fail. Need balance. Crew deaths, van breakdown, running out of fuel/food/water → game over. Reach Atlantic City → win.

Let's create a polished UI:
- Dark warm palette: cream/deep navy/rust/teal. Retro road-trip vibe, grain, sticker typography. Use system fonts? Google fonts may not load offline; can use local fallback stacks. Better avoid external network fonts for reliability. Use CSS font stacks: "Georgia" for display? A retro travel poster look. Use clamp with bold condensed sans. Maybe embed via Google Fonts? Network could be available in browser, but not guarantee. Use font-family with fallback; can load "Bebas Neue"/"DM Sans" from fonts.googleapis — risky. Instead use local stacks: Impact/Haettenschweiler for big headers? On Android those may not exist. Use system-ui + letter-spacing. For retro feel, SVG text? Let's design with strong layout instead of fonts.

Game screens:
1. Title: big "ROAD TO THE SHORE" / "ATLANTIC OR BUST". Tagline "San Francisco → Atlantic City. 2,867 miles. No second chances." Animated van on horizon, start button, how to play, best runs.
2. Crew select: 8 cards, choose exactly 4; each shows role, skill, perk, flaw. Starting van/equipment fixed. Show budget. "Roll out".
3. Road view (main): top status bar (day, miles, cash), van animation scene center, resource meters bottom. Log. A "Drive" primary button. At stop, "Enter town" modal/screen with services. Actually the flow:
   - Scene screen shows current location, next leg distance, animated road. Actions: "Drive to next stop" (choose pace?), "Camp" (if between stops? simpler: each stop = town screen).
   - Simpler robust loop: At town (start), you see town screen with shop/services/talk. Press "Hit the road" → a travel sequence to next stop with 1-2 events drawn. Events resolved via choice cards. Then arrive at next town. Last town = Atlantic City triggers win if arrive alive.
   - Travel costs fuel/food/water determined by distance and pace. Player chooses pace before travel (steady/fast/night drive) affecting resource burn and event risk.
4. Event screen: illustrated card, title, text, 2-3 choices with skill tags and odds. Resolve with animation and result text. Consequences.
5. Town screen: services — fuel up, grocery, water, mechanic, motel, clinic, pawn/sell, odd jobs for cash, trade. Each service with prices and effects. Also local "tip" and maybe a rumor. Press drive onward.
6. End screen: stats, cause of failure, miles, days, crew, obituary/epitaph, restart. Win screen big.

Need generated art. Use inline SVG scenes for events & background. Maybe a single SVG "poster" van. We can create a distinctive van (boxy 70s van) with luggage on top, side view, wheels. Animate slight bounce and wheel rotation, exhaust, road dashes moving. Parallax background layers: sky gradient, sun, mountains, cacti, town silhouettes. Different biomes per region: coast, desert, plains, city. We can implement scene as HTML/CSS with SVG.

I can generate a set of event illustrations using CSS/SVG mini-scenes (e.g., flat tire, storm, hitchhiker, roadblock, diner). That's a lot of art. Alternative: use a common illustrated "roadside vignette" with icons and color-coded event type; plus a big icon. I can hand-build ~12 SVG illustrations via reusable shapes. Maybe use emoji? Emoji can look cheap but effective if styled inside a scene. Better combine: event card hero uses a large line-art icon (SVG) over textured hazard-stripe background. Create icons for: engine, tire, fuel, water, food, money, weather, police, hitchhiker, motel, mechanic, radio, storm, bridge, desert sun, city. Use one SVG icon library with paths. Manageable.

Audio: optional Web Audio ambient engine hum, click, success/failure chimes, with mute toggle. Add subtle synth engine + road noise. Must be user-gesture initiated. Could be nice but not essential. I'll add simple tones and engine hum toggle.

Skills and checks:
- MECHANIC (Rosa) - repairs, engine checks
- MEDIC (Dr. Ellis) - injuries, illness
- NAVIGATOR (June) - route, shortcuts, avoid getting lost
- COOK (Marco) - stretches food, morale
- NEGOTIATOR (Ava) - prices, police, tolls
- SCOUT (Tomas) - finding supplies, weather
- ENTERTAINER (Cass) - morale, odd jobs, hitchhikers
- TECH (Priya) - electronics, van computer, radio, police scanner
Choose 4.

Each character: skill value (e.g., 1-3) used for checks, plus perk. Checks: roll d10 + skill*2 + modifiers vs difficulty; show probability. Maybe transparency: display "Mechanic check · 70%" on choices. This makes decisions meaningful. Also crew can be injured → skill unavailable/low until healed; morale influences all checks. Failing checks leads to resource loss; sometimes instant catastrophe at low condition.

Resources:
- Fuel: 0-100 (tank). Consumption per 100 miles ~ 18-25 units. Distance total ~ 2,900 miles. Stops every ~150-260 miles. Fuel price varies $3.20-$5.80/gal; abstract "units": tank 100, cost $2.40/unit maybe. Start cash $520. Need balance.
- Food: 0-100. Consumption/day based on crew count and rations setting (short/normal/hearty). Start 60.
- Water: 0-100. Similar.
- Van condition: 0-100. Breakdown events / bad roads reduce. At 0 → stranded → game over (unless repair).
- Morale: 0-100. Low morale triggers events, crew may leave; 0 → mutiny/game over.
- Cash: dollars. Start $600 maybe. Jobs earn $40-100, expenses. Selling equipment possible.
- Medicine kits: 0-3. Spare tire: 0-1. Jerry can: maybe fuel reserve 0-1 (20 fuel). Toolbox condition? Keep simpler: inventory items: medkit, spare tire, fuel can, snacks, toolkit, radio. Some characters grant items.
- Tires: separate 0-100? Could fold into condition. Keep "Tires" as wear 100-0 causing blowouts more likely. Maybe too much. Use condition + spare tire.

Equipment limited start: 1 spare tire, 2 medkits, 1 fuel can (20), toolbox, 3 days food/water? Resources abstract.

Daily/leg structure: Each leg = ~1 day (distance variable). Consume food/water per day. Pace choice modifies: 
- Easy (55 mph, +safety): fuel efficient? Actually slower = more days = more food/water, fewer breakdowns, better checks +1.
- Steady (normal)
- Push (75 mph): fewer days? Hmm distance-based days: day count increments 1 per leg regardless? Better: legs measured in miles, pace determines days and consumption. Each leg 200 miles: at 50mph = 4 days? That's a lot of days, but each stop several days. Oregon Trail has travel days. We can abstract: leg takes 1-2 days depending pace; choose "Take it easy", "Steady", "Push through the night". Resource consumption fixed per leg times pace modifier. Day counter increments pace-specific (easy 2 days, steady 1.5, push 1). Hmm long journey 12 stops → ~20 days. Fine.

Let's do each leg distance ~200-350 miles, and travel consumes:
- Fuel = distance * rate (0.055 per mile base = ~13-19 units) with condition/efficiency modifiers.
- Food/water = days * crew size; days = ceil(distance / (mph*10))? Let's make pace:
  - Cruise (safe): days 2, fuel ×0.9, risk low, check +1
  - Steady: days 1.5→2? Hmm.
Let's simplify to per-leg consumption with clearly displayed preview: "Fuel -22 · Food -14 · Water -12 · 2 days". Pace modifies.

Total route: SF→Sacramento(88)→Reno(218)→Salt Lake City(518)→Cheyenne(432)→Omaha(500)→Chicago(470)→Cleveland(345)→Pittsburgh(135)→Philadelphia(305)→Atlantic City(65). Totals ~3076 miles. Great. 9 legs. Add St. Louis? Route through Denver? Let's choose a classic interstate route: SF → Sacramento → Reno → Salt Lake City → Cheyenne → Omaha → Chicago → Cleveland → Pittsburgh → Philadelphia → Atlantic City. 10 stops, last arrival. Each leg 88-500 miles. 500 mi in one leg might consume lots. Could break Salt Lake→Cheyenne into Salt Lake→Rawlins→Cheyenne for more stops. Stops:
1. San Francisco (start)
2. Sacramento 88
3. Reno 218 (via I-80)
4. Elko 300
5. Salt Lake City 230
6. Rawlins 310
7. Cheyenne 290
8. Omaha 500 (long)
9. Chicago 470
10. Cleveland 345
11. Pittsburgh 135
12. Philadelphia 305
13. Atlantic City 65
Total ≈ 3256 mi. 12 travel legs. That's a good length for a 30-45 min run. Most runs fail.

Maybe shorten for mobile: 9 legs, total ~2,900. Use: SF→Sacramento (88), →Reno (218), →Salt Lake City (518), →Cheyenne (432), →Omaha (500), →Chicago (470), →Cleveland (345), →Pittsburgh (135), →Philadelphia (305), →Atlantic City (65). Total 3,076. 9 legs. Long legs.

Resources scale: fuel tank 100 usable ~ 520 miles at 5.2 units/100mi? Let's set fuel consumption ~ 6.5 units per 100 miles base → 500-mile leg = 32.5 units. Tank 100. Stops every leg so refuel opportunities. Start fuel 72 (not full). Cost per unit ~$1.35 → fill 100 costs $135. Start cash ~$740. Income from odd jobs and selling. Food/water consumption per day per person: food 1.6 units/person/day, water 2 units/person/day; 4 crew × 1.5 days × 1.6 = ~10 per leg. Start food 55, water 55; capacity 100. Groceries $1.2/unit food, water $0.5/unit. Days ~1-3 per leg (distance/250 approx + pace). This gives manageable but tight economy.

Condition: starts 78. Each leg base wear 3-7, events add 10-30. Repairs cost $60+parts and mechanic skill. Condition 0 = catastrophic breakdown → failure unless fix with spare parts and successful mechanic check (dramatic). Tires: random blowout events. Maybe fold.

Morale: starts 70. Drops from low food/water, failures, bad events; rises from hearty rations, diners, entertainment, scenic stops. Morale modifies checks ±; 0 → crew abandons → fail.

Win: reach Atlantic City with at least one crew member alive and van condition > 0. Arrival triggers final "The boardwalk" scene. Score based on cash, crew, day. Endings: "Made it" or "Stranded in..." with obituary.

Difficulty: "challenging" – tune event failure consequences and prices to be punishing. Add easy mode? Request says challenging and most runs fail. Include "Story" difficulty? Maybe only one difficulty, plus optional "Assist mode"? Don't undermine. Could have "Standard" only. Maybe unlock an easier "Sunday Drive" after first completion for accessibility; not necessary.

Narrative: A road trip to Atlantic City because a band/company? Premise: You're driving to Atlantic City for the "All-American Road Rally" or to deliver a demo tape to a record label? Let's craft: "Four strangers. One tired van. A shot at the biggest battle of the bands on the Atlantic City boardwalk." But skills mechanic/medic etc. fits a crew. Van name "The Albatross". Goal: get the crew to Atlantic City for a $20,000 prize / a fresh start. Unique skills. Maybe "You have 21 days to reach the boardwalk" adds time pressure — a deadline. Great: "The Boardwalk Invitational" — a cross-country scavenger rally? Or a friend's wedding? Let's make it a legendary cross-country road rally "The Cannonball" with a $10,000 purse at the finish, and you're a ragtag crew in a 1978 van. Narrative: "Your band got a last-minute slot at the Atlantic City Battle of the Bands on Labor Day. The van is packed, the rent is due, and nobody has a plan B." Each character has a reason. This gives morale and entertainment relevance.

Time limit: 24 days. Each leg takes 1-3 days. Total maybe 20 days at steady pace; pushing saves days but costs condition/morale. This adds a strategic tradeoff. Deadline creates failure (miss the show → game over). 3,076 miles over 24 days = 128 mi/day average, but legs adjust. Let's compute days per leg = distance/220 rounded, modified by pace: cruise +1 day, steady base, sprint -1 (min 1). Base days sum: 88/220=.4→1, 218→1, 518→3, 432→2, 500→3, 470→3, 345→2, 135→1, 305→2, 65→1 = 19 days. Plus start day 1. 24-day deadline leaves 4-5 days slack, but repairs/rest add days at stops (each town action consumes maybe 0 extra unless rest/job = +1 day). Good tension. Pushing reduces days by 1 per leg (min 1) → total 14, but more risk. Cruise +1 → 27, fails unless sprint. Nice.

Let's make town actions: 
- Refuel (instant, no day)
- Buy supplies (instant)
- Repair at garage: costs cash + 1 day (or self-repair: mechanic check + 0 day but risk)
- Rest at motel: $45 +1 day, morale +15, heal injuries
- Work a gig: +1 day, earn cash (skill-based)
- Clinic: heal for cash, +1 day? Maybe instant treatment, 1 day recovery.
Each town has rumors/tips, price variations, local event. Keeping each town unique with a short note and a special service (e.g., Reno casino gamble, Cheyenne rodeo job, Chicago deep dish morale).

Event system: Deck of ~40 events, weighted by region and conditions. Each event has:
- id, title, art icon, text, region tags, choices.
Choices: label, skill (role or "any"), difficulty, outcomes (success/fail), requirements (cash/item/crew). Some risk-free choices with basic cost. Skill check probability shown. If skill owner injured → skill check uses lower? Injured crew can't use skill (or -2). Crew can die; their skill lost. Death perhaps from severe failures. Need careful: most runs fail, but deaths should be possible and meaningful. Injured characters: "banged up" → checks with their skill -2. Healing at clinic/motel over days.

I'll implement characters with skill level 1-3:
- Rosa "Wrench" Alvarez — Mechanic 3. Perk: repairs 35% cheaper, starts with toolbox. Flaw: stubborn; morale drops on retreat? Keep simple perks.
- Dr. Nell Okafor — Medic 3. Perk: medkits heal more, starts +1 medkit. 
- June Park — Navigator 3. Perk: fuel use -8%, shortcut events. 
- Marco Bellini — Cook 3. Perk: food consumption -20%, morale from meals.
- Ava Sloane — Negotiator 3. Perk: shop prices -12%, better police/toll outcomes.
- Tomás Reyes — Scout 3. Perk: find supplies on the road, better weather outcomes.
- Cass "Kaz" Ibarra — Entertainer 2/3. Perk: +morale each day, gigs pay +50%.
- Priya Nair — Tech 3. Perk: police scanner, detects road hazards, engine tuning + fuel efficiency.

Each skill used in events. Characters have "bonds"? Maybe too complex. Add small relationship/morale flavor via "campfire" choices. Keep scope.

Selection: choose 4 from 8. Each has portrait (SVG avatar, geometric). Skill distribution matters. Make portraits distinct with color palettes and simple shapes. Use CSS/SVG.

Checks: d10 + skill*2 + moraleBonus (morale>70 +1, <30 -1) vs difficulty (8-14). Display % probability computed. On success good; failure consequences. Some choices guaranteed costs.

Balance math:
- skill 3 → +6, difficulty 10 → roll 4+ = 70%. skill 2 → 60%, skill 1 → 50%. With assist +1. Difficulties: 9 (easy), 11 (medium), 13 (hard). At skill 3: 90/70/50. Without skill: use raw d10 + 0: 20/10/0? Actually "no skill" base 1 + d10? Let's define check: 1d10 + skill rank*2 + morale mod. Unskilled uses d10 (skill 0). Hard 13 impossible unskilled. Good. Players need right crew.

Morale effect: -1 if <30, +1 if >75.

Pace modifies check by +1 or -1? Cautious +1, push -1.

Skills can be used proactively at town:
- Self repair (Mechanic)
- Forage (Scout) for food/water
- Busk (Entertainer) cash
- Hustle/negotiate (Negotiator) sell item / discount
- Tune van (Tech) fuel efficiency buff
- Cook a feast (Cook) morale
- Triage (Medic) heal injury with medkit
- Route plan (Navigator) choose better route next leg (less fuel / avoid event)

Maybe that's the "crew actions" screen at each town — each character can do one job once per town, each costs a day? Too many days. Better: town has 4 slots? Keep simple: town action menu includes services and "Crew actions" where each available character's special action can be performed once per town, costing 1 day total (not per action) or no day. Limit days: 24-day deadline. If each town 3-4 actions cost days, too many. So make most actions no time; only "Rest", "Work", "Repair shop", "Clinic" cost a day. Character perks are passive + event options. Add "Camp" between towns? 

Travel loop with an interstitial "On the road" scene: after choosing pace, show animated driving for a moment, then draw event. Each leg triggers 1-2 events (based on distance). Then arrival. The sequence:
1. From town, tap "Hit the road" → pace modal (or pace selector on town screen) → animate road, day advances, resources consumed, then event 1 (if any) → resolve → maybe event 2 → arrival screen summary with town.
2. On arrival, town panel with services and "Roll out".

For mobile: one screen at a time, thumb-friendly buttons at bottom. Safe-area insets.

Persistence: localStorage for best distance/runs and maybe save current run. Add auto-save to localStorage so refresh resumes; "Continue" on title. Should implement to be polished. Save state after every action.

Accessibility: large tap targets, contrast, reduced motion support, mute.

Testing: Use playwright-cli per instructions with screenshots. Need server on port 3000 or 3002. I'll run `python3 -m http.server 3000` in tmux? Agents.md says use tmux persistent. Check tmux availability. Then use playwright-cli. Need figure its commands. Let me inspect help.

## Objective
- Complete a playable, mobile-friendly Oregon Trail-inspired browser game about traveling by van from San Francisco to Atlantic City.

## Requirements
- Include crew with distinct skills, limited equipment, and challenging resource- and skill-based events; most runs should fail.
- Support phones and tablets.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finishing.
- Save small JPEG screenshots for checks at viewport widths no greater than 1280px, and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use a self-contained responsive HTML/CSS/JavaScript game with crew selection, travel pace, resource management, event choices, persistent saves, and win/failure outcomes.
- The crew begins with four selected friends from five available; steady and fast paces trade speed for wear and risk.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game structure, illustrated route, responsive styling, bundled fonts, events, resources, save/load, and end states in `index.html`, `styles.css`, and `game.js`.
- Added a no-op data favicon to eliminate the initial missing `/favicon.ico` console error.
- Fixed event handling so resource shortages disable unaffordable options, success-only resource gains apply and are reported, and the Utah crossing’s `time` delta no longer silently disappears.
- Adjusted resource consumption and added supply sources at Nevada, Kansas, and Illinois.
- `node --check game.js` passes; browser reload reports no console errors.
- Captured and inspected `/tmp/opencode/mobile-setup.jpg` at 390×844; setup screen rendered.

### Active
- Continue testing routes, mobile layout, resource edges, save/reload, and win/failure states; adjust balance based on playthroughs.
- Capture and inspect a fresh latest JPEG screenshot (viewport ≤1280px).

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Retest a full run after the latest resource-consumption adjustment, including event-choice affordability and failure behavior.
2. Verify setup and active gameplay at phone and desktop viewports, plus save/reload and ending states.
3. Save and inspect a current small JPEG screenshot, then summarize assumptions and verification results.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game content, resource balance, event logic, persistence, and outcomes.
- `index.html`: Page structure and illustrated landscape.
- `styles.css`: Desktop and mobile/tablet layouts.
- `assets/fonts/`: Bundled Archivo Black and Space Grotesk fonts.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Local server is running at `http://localhost:3002`; Playwright CLI is installed and Chromium was installed for testing.
- Initial mobile screenshot at `/tmp/opencode/mobile-setup.jpg` predates the latest gameplay adjustments.

## Objective
- Complete a playable, mobile-friendly Oregon Trail-inspired browser game about traveling by van from San Francisco to Atlantic City.

## Requirements
- Include crew with distinct skills, limited equipment, and challenging resource- and skill-based events; most runs should fail.
- Support phones and tablets.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finishing.
- Save small JPEG screenshots for checks at viewport widths no greater than 1280px, and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Objective
- Complete a playable, mobile-friendly Oregon Trail-inspired browser game about traveling by van from San Francisco to Atlantic City.

## Requirements
- Include a crew with distinct skills, limited equipment, and challenging resource- and skill-based events; most runs should fail.
- Support phones and tablets.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finishing.
- Save small JPEG screenshots at viewport widths no greater than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use a self-contained responsive HTML/CSS/JavaScript game with crew selection, travel pace, resource management, event choices, persistent saves, and win/failure outcomes.
- The crew begins with four selected friends from five available; steady and fast paces trade speed for wear and risk.
- Added a no-supplies Appalachians option to avoid event dead ends; its outcome risks van condition and morale.
- Set food/water consumption to `2.8` per 70 miles to retain a high failure rate while allowing some wins.

### Completed
- Implemented game structure, illustrated route, responsive styling, bundled fonts, events, resources, save/load, and win/failure outcomes.

2. Run syntax and responsive checks, including the latest screenshot capture/inspection if the layout changes.

- `game.js`: Events, resource balance, save/load, and outcomes.
- `index.html`: Game structure and illustrated landscape.
- `styles.css`: Desktop and mobile/tablet layouts.
